news.title: Women Have Always Shaped America
news.text:
American women flexed their political muscles in the 2026 election, participating as voters and candidates, influencing outcomes, and breaking records by sending more women than ever to hold statewide elected office. Several states elected female governors for the first time. Women aren’t a monolithic voting bloc, but they are a powerful force in American politics. 

This has been true since the beginning. Our country would not be what it is today without the contributions of countless women — some of whom are widely recognized in history books, but many of whom are not. This Thanksgiving holiday, we should reflect on all the freedoms and privileges we have as American women and the debt of gratitude we owe to those who came before us.

During the American Revolution, women organized boycotts of British goods, raised money for the cause, supplied soldiers in encampments, and worked as cooks, laundresses, and nurses alongside the men. Some women even acted as spies. Elizabeth Burgin, a mother of three, helped more than 200 American prisoners of war escape from the British. Women like Margaret Corbin and Mary Ludwig Hays (also known as "Molly Pitcher") even loaded and fired field cannons after their husbands fell in battle.

Throughout the 19th century, women shaped our young country. Although their direct political influence was limited, the importance of their indirect influence cannot be overstated. For example, Dolley Madison transformed the office of the First Lady into a proactive role and used her position to bring people together. She may be remembered most for hosting parties, but the result of her efforts was greater bipartisanship. 

In the 1830s, Alexis de Tocqueville toured America and made observations about our democracy, comparing and contrasting it to Europe. He had a lot to say about American women, and essentially credited them with the success of our vibrant civil society. He wrote: “I have nowhere seen woman occupying a loftier position; and if I were asked…to what the singular prosperity and growing strength of that people ought mainly to be attributed, I should reply: To the superiority of their women.”

Around this same time, a woman named Sarah Josepha Hale was a writer and editor for ladies’ magazines. By today’s standards, she might not be considered a feminist because she strongly believed that women’s primary sphere was domestic life, but she advocated for new opportunities for women, including in higher education. Before and during the Civil War, she petitioned five different American presidents, asking them to establish the national holiday of Thanksgiving. Like Dolley Madison, she understood that there was power in bringing people together around a table.

Later in the 19th century, Harriet Tubman would lead dozens of slaves to freedom on the Underground Railroad. Other women, like Sojourner Truth, Lucretia Mott, and Sarah and Angelina Grimké, and many others were leaders in the movement to abolish slavery. 

Many people know the suffrage movement of the early 20th century resulted in the 19th Amendment, guaranteeing women the right to vote nationwide in 1920 (thanks to women like Susan B. Anthony and Elizabeth Cady Stanton). But some don’t know that Wyoming was the first place to recognize women’s suffrage, in 1869 while it was still just a territory. The state of Montana became the first state to elect a woman to Congress, Rep. Jeannette Rankin, in 1916.

In the 1940s and throughout World War II, women’s roles evolved to meet the needs of a nation at war. “Rosie the Riveter” became symbolic of women who took on traditionally masculine roles. They welded ships, built tanks, assembled bombs, operated heavy machinery, and worked as scientists, code breakers, and engineers in the war effort. In the private sector, millions of women entered the workforce during this time, keeping the economy going while the troops were fighting abroad. 

The latter part of the 20th century and the first part of the 21st century have seen enormous progress, and countless glass ceilings have shattered. Women like Ella Baker and Rosa Parks made invaluable contributions to the civil rights movement of the 1960s. Sandra Day O’Connor became the first female supreme court justice in 1981. Sally Ride became the first American woman to go to outer space in 1983. Kamala Harris became the first female vice president of the United States in 2021. 

All along, we’ve had political debates about the status of women and the roles we should play. While many women achieve greatness in their professions, many more make contributions to their families, neighborhoods, and communities through consistent acts of service and love. We may not always “have it all” if that means having the perfect work-life balance. But we do have the freedom to make choices, to participate as citizens, and to pursue happiness as we see fit. 

America should be proud of its women. And American women should be proud of our country. This Thanksgiving, I’m thankful for the women who’ve come before me, and I’m committed to serving my country, as they did, and paying it forward to those who’ll come after me. 

Hadley Heath Manning is a senior fellow at Independent Women.

news.title: Ben & Jerry’s Is Super Thankful for the Violence of Abortion
news.text:
What does ice cream have to do with abortion?

Absolutely nothing. But that never stopped Ben & Jerry’s founders, Ben Cohen and Jerry Greenfield, from churning milk into frothy abortion activism. You name the far-left cause, they were on the bandwagon. Perhaps they were even driving it. What’s fascinating to me is how two white Jewish men think that abortion needs to happen more in black communities where abortion is already the number one killer of black lives. Which flavor would that be, anyway? Genocide with Chunks of Racism? 

Of course, Ben & Jerry’s calls it “Reproductive Justice.” Civil rights icon Fannie Lou Hamer called it “genocide.” Jesse Jackson (before he ran for president on the Democrat ticket) called it “genocide.” Dr. Alveda King, niece of Dr. Martin Luther King, calls it “crime against humanity” and “racist.” What is just about disproportionately killing the most marginalized black lives?

Ben & Jerry’s declared their fake war on white supremacy in 2024 (ironically the very thing that past and present abortion workers accuse Planned Parenthood of): “…the culture of white supremacy must be dismantled to achieve equity for all marginalized people. We have focused our strategies on outcomes for Black people because slavery and its legacy remain such a defining element of American life.”

Abortion is one of slavery’s sordid legacies. Dr. Mildred Jefferson, the first black woman to graduate from Harvard Medical School (and first female surgeon at Boston Medical), explained this: “I would guess that the abortionists have done more to get rid of generations and cripple others than all of the years of slavery and lynchings.”

Ben & Jerry’s apparently thinks limitless abortion should always be on the menu, as it declares on its website: “Roe was always meant to be the floor — not the ceiling — for abortion rights.”

Empower Mint

In the company’s relatively new podcast, Into the Mix, it heavily pushes abortion propaganda disguising it as liberation and empowerment. The episode, entitled “Liberating Abortion,” features Ashley C. Ford, a self-described lesbian and New York Times bestselling author, as well as abortion activist Renee Bracey Sherman. The entire podcast centers on disinformation and the importance of “abortion storytelling.” Sherman repeatedly describes the failure of telling good emotional stories, while her own storytelling is painfully bland and filled with meaningless word salads.

In true Kamala Harris style, Sherman unleashes a tirade of words at war with one another to sum up her worldview at the start of the podcast: “It’s truly at the core of my views on abortion and making sure that everyone has access to safe and healthy pregnancy care but also my view of the world in that every child, every baby, every mama, every parent, every trans person, everyone deserves the healthcare that is most affirming to them and that they get it when they need it.”

She never once mentioned prenatal care in the podcast. Virtually zero Planned Parenthoods offer it (it’s less than 0.1 percent of its services). Being dismembered, sucked out with an aspiration machine, or snuffed out with a DIY chemical abortion pill is not affirming for any child.

The gist of Sherman’s story is that she had a crappy boyfriend that she regularly had sex with during her early years in college. She was 19, allegedly worked at Victoria’s Secret, and didn’t have enough money to get (low-cost, often no-cost) birth control pills. There were numerous contradictions in her story. In the podcast version, she claimed the abortion cost $450. In her 2016 op-ed in Women’s Health magazine, it was $350. She also told the host that she only had a credit card with a max of $500, yet she somehow paid for the $450 abortion and the $100 “twilight sedation” charge on that same card? Somehow, her math ain’t mathin’.

In the podcast, she claimed she sat alone in the abortion mill and wished she had someone there supporting her. She never mentioned, as she did in the op-ed, that her boyfriend took her there and, though he initially wanted them to choose adoption, he backed her abortion decision — until they arrived there. The Ben & Jerry’s remix of this part is typical of “abortion storyselling.” They demonized anyone who opposes abortion, falsely smeared pregnancy centers who help millions, and ignored the fact that loving the post-abortive doesn’t mean affirming the violence done to them.

Sherman boasted in both the podcast and her op-ed about how “progressive” her parents were and accepting of abortion. In the article, she proclaimed: “Abortion was never out of the question. I grew up in a politically progressive family where it was a sin to not vote or not have an opinion on an issue…While we may not have talked about abortion in a very in-depth way, I knew from a young age that our family stood with Planned Parenthood and that my mother felt abortion was a reasonable option.” Then why was it hard to go to them?

At one point in the same article, she mentioned that her boyfriend would have “sex with her while she was asleep.” Um. Normally, people would call this rape. Bizarrely, it didn’t deserve such recognition from Sherman.

One Sweet Whirled

“I wasn’t ready to parent. And to be honest, I simply didn’t want to be pregnant.” Sherman’s story — true or not — sadly, is not unique. My wife, Bethany, understands the same feelings of not being ready to parent. In her 20s, she found herself in a toxic relationship, walked away, and within weeks found out that she was pregnant. The economics weren’t right. The guy wasn’t right. The timing wasn’t right. But killing her unborn child wasn’t right regardless of the circumstances. Bethany rejected the violence of abortion.

Ben & Jerry’s wants us to believe that the world is sweeter when we kill our offspring. Every one of its flavors is tainted with the bitter taste of abortion extremism. I scream, you scream, we (should) all scream for life-affirming ice cream.

news.title: Thanksgrifting
news.text:
The losers who don’t know how to give thanks.

Mossad folks tend to keep their mouths shut — that’s part of their business. My wife’s cousin used to point out where their office is while saying that it was forbidden to point out where their office was. So it was a bit of a surprise when former Mossad chief David Barnea casually mentioned that it was his outfit that prevented an ISIS attack at a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. According to his explanation, the Austrians provided raw intelligence which the Mossad “processed” and helped to bring an end to the plot and the arrest of the terrorists. This is a beautiful example of how things are supposed to work. Unfortunately, Israel is one big one-way street, both when I drive around here and in the world at large.

After the announcement that Israel helped prevent a repeat of the Manchester Arena bombing, I would have expected Taylor Swift to put out a statement thanking the Mossad for its efforts to keep her fans safe. And maybe she made a private call to Binyamin Netanyahu and offered five discs as her form of thanks. But thanks from lefties are rare. They feel totally entitled, and anything done for them was deserved, earned, and expected. Swift is wealthy, talented, and also smart. She knows that if she were to thank Israel, she would anger her mostly lefty fan base. What is it worth saying thanks if the paying customers will stop buying her music and merchandise? Remember when she threw her support to Kamala Harris? How did a reelected Donald Trump repay her? He congratulated her on the announcement of her engagement to football star Travis Kelce. Trump is in another league compared to the ingrates on the left.

Thanksgiving was always beloved — lots of family, food, and football. A long weekend and then...shopping. I was in the open market “shuk” recently and saw a big turkey at one of the local butchers. It was waiting for its American patron to buy it. “Jews” are called in Hebrew, “Yehudim”, from the name of the fourth son of Jacob, Yehuda. The root of this name is “Hoda’a” which means thanks. Not far from my house is Rechov (street in Hebrew) George Washington. At the end of it, you will find Rechov Abraham Lincoln. Not far outside of Jerusalem, one can find a quiet, pastoral place in the John F. Kennedy Forest. The first street one hits when arriving in Tel Aviv has always been Laguardia. There are three 9/11 memorials in Israel — and not because of the Israelis or even the Jews who were killed on that day. It is a testament to the bond that Israel feels for America and the American people. A friend of mine who was no great fan of Donald Trump had only praise when the president returned to the White House and began sending war material that had been held up by the Biden administration.

Giving thanks at a minimum requires a person to peer outside of himself. If one believes that he either deserves or has earned everything, then why should he say, “thank you”? If someone paid a lot of money for a flight, why should he thank the flight attendant who brings his dinner? On the one hand, he paid for the meal as part of the price of his ticket. On the other hand, he can show some appreciation towards another human being who did his or her best to make life just a little bit more pleasant. She could throw the food tray at him, or they could announce that people can pick up the food on their own. One thing you almost never see from the left or their Muslim friends is gratitude. It’s always complaints, accusations, and demands. They are the most miserable people enjoying the highest standard of living ever created on this planet. It’s a farce to see some anti-fossil fuel ninny or Jew-hating ogre using an iPhone. Israel probably has some tech in it, and coal/oil were used in its manufacture and transport to market. These people are deranged narcissists and can’t see beyond the end of their noses.

While I am glad that a potential attack in Austria was averted, one has to call a time-out and really think about this arrangement. Ireland is competing with Spain and France to be the most antisemitic, Israel-hating country in Europe. Their “leaders” ran to recognize a nonexistent country, “Palestine,” as a reward for Hamas’ murder of 1,200 Israelis. They never stop accusing Israel of genocide and starving the fat Gazan population. They even wanted to remove the name of a former Israeli president and son of the Emerald Isle — and father of the current Israeli president — from a Dublin Park. But, lo and behold, despite a threatened boycott of Israeli tech, Irish police bought an Israeli anti-drone system. My feeling is that there comes a time to stop helping one’s enemies.

Israel famously removed a brain tumor from Yahya Sinwar, so that he could turn around and orchestrate the mass murder of Jews on October 7, 2023. At what point does Israel identify friends like the US, help them, and remember enemies and tell them to pound sand? Does Israel somehow have a moral obligation to help its enemies? Let’s say that it uncovers a plot through signal intelligence of a plan to blow up a major tower in Riyadh. Does Israel have to pass along this information to the Saudis via the US? Can’t they just buy a lot of popcorn and wait for it to happen? On the one hand, it was obviously good that the planned attack at the Swift concert did not occur. On the other hand, what has Austria done to reduce the anti-Israel hatred in Europe? Why is Israel always driving on one-way streets with unfriendly countries? Israel provides intelligence, tech, and sometimes manpower — like in earthquakes. And all she receives in return are complaints, threats, and boycotts.

One of the more difficult aspects of World War II involved the work at Bletchley Park. There were many plans and attacks that the code-breakers there discovered prior to their occurrence. When the British could send a plane or ship to “accidentally” discover the plans, they would. But there were cases where, under the orders of Winston Churchill, Allied soldiers and sailors died in order to prevent the Germans from knowing that their codes had been broken. I am sure that these were not easy decisions — to sacrifice men and equipment so that they could continue to decipher messages. Estimates say that the work on the Enigma and other coding machines may have reduced the length of the war by a year or two.

So should Israel send Spain anti-terror tech or critical intelligence? What is the difference between sending some high-tech military gear to France or Iran? Why does Israel provide intelligence to countries like England that blackball its native companies? Will Israel ever get over its battered wife syndrome and start telling its former friends and partners to go pound sand or show public gratitude? Send them flowers before the funerals, and maybe they will come to their senses: choose between the left/Muslim death spiral or work with Israel to be safe and prosperous.

Israel apparently warned the Trump administration of Iranian plans to harm top administration officials. This is the way it should work: Israel is grateful and helps its big friend. I don’t know if it needs to be so forthcoming to losers and ingrates like the leaders of Europe. Churchill didn’t enjoy hiding England’s knowledge, but he did it for a greater good. Israel might wish to learn from him. Reward your friends and let your enemies fend for themselves.

news.title: For Trump, doubling down on tariffs is about power, not popularity
news.text:
PALM BEACH - In midterm elections three weeks ago, US voters punished Republicans over an economy and inflation that many said were made worse by tariffs. President Donald Trump is doubling down on them anyway.

The Trump administration on Nov 25 announced a new round of tariffs on goods from 14 major trading ​partners, including China, Japan and the European Union, a seemingly counterintuitive move that reflects both Trump’s decades-old belief in tariffs and a new political reality confronting his White House.

With Democrats set to control Congress for the final two years of his presidency, tariffs are taking on added importance as one of the most potent economic tools Trump can wield without lawmakers’ approval.

Tariffs are taxes levied on imports, raising costs for consumers. But Trump sees them as a way to wring concessions from foreign leaders, force corporate CEOs to build plants in the US, raise cash for the government and curry favour with blue-collar voters, according to US officials and other people familiar with the president’s thinking.

And after a midterm defeat for his party that threatens to sharply constrain his domestic agenda, Trump is eager to demonstrate that he remains capable of driving economic policy and exercising power even as his legislative clout diminishes, the people said.

“This is all because of tariffs,” Trump told CNBC on Nov 23 as he touted new factories being built in the US. But he said the policy could come with costs. “There’s going to be always that little headache during this little transition period.”

Some Republicans in Congress were quick to blame the president’s tariff policy for the party’s stunning midterm losses. Two-thirds of voters said Trump’s tariff policies hurt the national economy, compared with 21% who said they had helped and 12% who found no difference, according to exit polls conducted by SSRS on behalf of a consortium of US media outlets. Yale University’s Budget Lab estimated earlier in November that tariffs raised US household costs by US$900 (S$1,161) annually.

The administration nevertheless proposed new tariffs that would increase duties on targeted imports, with maximum rates of 20% to 40%, though completed or pending trade deals would generally limit them to 10% to 20%.

The new policy, which followed an eight-month review of trading partners’ practices, revamps a set of tariffs that Trump imposed in 2025 and the Supreme Court struck down as illegal in February.

Trump’s chief trade negotiator, Jamieson Greer, made the tariff announcement with little fanfare on the eve of the US Thanksgiving holiday. Trump himself made no public remarks on the new actions, a marked contrast with his “Liberation Day” tariff announcement in 2025 in the White House Rose Garden.

Despite the muted rollout, the market reaction was swift, with the benchmark S&P 500 closing down a quarter of a percentage point on Nov 25.

Trump had also roiled the markets just days earlier with his extraordinary efforts to restore Jensen Huang as CEO of the chipmaker Nvidia, a surprise move that tested the bounds of presidential intervention in private markets. Stock markets rallied on Huang’s return, but have since pared back.

Concerns about affordability

Democrats seized on the tariff announcement, saying Trump was willfully ignoring voters’ anger about high costs and inflation, which have also been fueled by Trump’s decision to attack Iran, sparking a conflict that has significantly disrupted oil production and shipping. Several Democrats also argued that, by punishing allies, the policy did little to thwart China’s aggressive trade practices.

“Republicans have learned nothing,” incoming House Majority Leader Katherine Clark, a Massachusetts Democrat, said on X.

A former senior US trade official who served under Trump said the midterm rout likely moderated the tariff rates proposed, given that stiffer rates could trigger fresh concerns over affordability.

But while the election focused heavily on rising fuel prices and the cost of living, Trump has made reducing the US trade deficit a cornerstone of his administration, arguing that Washington was effectively shipping factory jobs overseas.

“Putting a stop to American workers, farmers, and businesses being ripped off by lopsided trade agreements has been a key foundation of President Trump’s Make America Great Again movement,” said White House spokesman Matthew Middleton, adding that the administration would “continue fighting to lower costs”.

Tariffs also have brought a new revenue source to the federal government after Trump’s signature 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act cemented lower individual tax rates.

Trump’s protectionist policies have drawn support from some blue-collar labor groups that historically backed Democrats, even as some Republicans recoil from an economic tool they view as hostile to free markets.

United Steelworkers International President Roxanne Brown on Wednesday called the administration’s actions “long overdue”. The group endorsed Trump’s Democratic opponent, Kamala Harris, in 2024.

Republican US Representative Don Bacon of Nebraska, a Trump critic who is retiring from Congress, took a different view. Calling tariffs “a tax on American consumers” and blaming high inflation and lower wage growth for Republicans’ losses, he urged lawmakers to reclaim authority over import duties. REUTERS

Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville warned that California Gov. He's got a huge fundraising base. There's no doubt about it," Carville said. "His problem is, 'Are we going to do this California s--- again? Really? Is that what we're going to do?'"

news.title: Maine Democrat Senator-Elect Troy Jackson Backs Chris Van Hollen to Oust Chuck Schumer as Majority Leader
news.text:
Sen.-elect Troy Jackson (D-ME), a longtime skeptic of Senate Democrat Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), announced Wednesday that he will vote for Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) in the upcoming Senate Democrat leadership election, citing their shared support for eliminating the filibuster, passing Medicare for All, and increasing the minimum wage.

Jackson, who defeated longtime Republican Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME) in the November midterm elections, announced his decision in a November 25 statement ahead of the December 1 secret ballot to determine who will lead Democrats’ incoming 56-seat Senate majority.

“I’ve talked with Mainers about what they need from the Senate, and I believe it’s time for a change in leadership. I’ll be voting for Senator Van Hollen. When we spoke, I told him Maine needs a seat at the table when the caucus decides what gets funded and what we’re going to fight for. I was impressed by his vision for the caucus, and I came away confident he’ll take Maine’s priorities seriously,” Jackson stated.

“From one end of Maine to the other, I heard the same thing. People are working harder, falling further behind, and getting tired of being told to wait. Senator Van Hollen and I agree that it’s time to end the filibuster, pass Medicare for All, and give working people a raise by increasing the minimum wage. I want a leader who’ll bring those fights to the floor,” he continued.

“Mainers voted for change in November, and they ought to get it. Whoever leads this caucus, I’ll fight like hell to make sure the Senate takes on the problems Mainers sent me to Washington to solve,” Jackson concluded.

Jackson’s endorsement comes as an Economist/YouGov poll conducted November 20–23 found that Democrats surveyed preferred Van Hollen over Schumer by 21 percentage points, 40 percent to 19 percent, while 2024 Kamala Harris voters surveyed favored the Maryland Democrat by 30 points, 48 percent to 18 percent. During a Sunday appearance on NBC’s Meet the Press, Van Hollen expressed confidence that he could secure the 28 votes needed to defeat Schumer, citing the endorsement of Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-MI). “We’re north of 15 and momentum is in our direction,” he said. During a November 15 appearance on ABC’s This Week, Van Hollen accused Schumer’s team of spreading “misinformation” and “trying to instill fear in people who may say that they’re going to support me as a new leader.”

Approximately 35 Hollywood figures, including Jane Fonda and Robert De Niro, have also signed a letter urging Senate Democrats to replace Schumer, according to a New York Times report covered by Breitbart News Tuesday. Comedian Jon Stewart and Marvel actor Mark Ruffalo have notably advocated a leadership change. Ruffalo subsequently faced accusations of antisemitism after calling for leadership that followed “the will of the people not entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties,” defending his remarks by citing Schumer’s 2018 AIPAC speech and calling for the consistent enforcement of domestic and international law.

Jackson, a former Maine Senate president and majority leader, defeated Collins in the November 3 election, denying the Republican a sixth term. NBC News projections showed Jackson leading Collins 52.6 percent to 47.3 percent when she reportedly called to concede. “I called Troy Jackson tonight to congratulate him and to assure him that my staff and I will work to ensure a smooth transition,” Collins stated, according to Punchbowl News senior congressional reporter Andrew Desiderio. 

Democrats backed Jackson after their initial candidate, Graham Platner, who faced scrutiny over a Nazi tattoo, exited the race following allegations of sexual misconduct and rape. Jackson’s campaign also faced scrutiny over allegations that his longtime partner is his second cousin.

Former Sen. Joe Manchin (I-WV), who supported Collins’ reelection campaign, argued during an October appearance on NewsNation’s The Hill that Jackson’s decision to campaign alongside prominent progressives reflected how he would govern. “Bernie and AOC and Elizabeth, I doubt they ever knew the other opponent, Susan’s opponent, up there. And they come from the far left of the Democratic Party,” Manchin said, adding that the people a candidate chooses to campaign alongside indicate “where you’re going to go and how you’re going to vote and represent your state.”

news.title: Houston in talks to host Essence Fest after New Orleans departure
news.text:
The city of Houston, Texas, says it is in talks to host the Essence Festival of Culture, after festival organizers announced this week that the annual event was leaving its longtime host city of New Orleans after more than 30 years.

"With confirmation this week that the event is leaving New Orleans, we can confirm that Houston has been in direct talks with Sundial Media Group, the owner of Essence, to bring the festival to our city," Houston Mayor John Whitmire said Wednesday in a joint statement with Houston First Corporation President and CEO Michael Heckman. "Those discussions have accelerated significantly in recent weeks."

VIDEO: 2025 Essence Festival spotlights Disney, Hulu, and Nat Geo in New Orleans 

The mayor said his team is "encouraged by the possibilities" of what Essence Festival would look like if it was brought to Texas and touted Houston's "rich Black cultural heritage."

The organizers of Essence Festival, which takes places every year over the Fourth of July weekend, previously announced in a letter Tuesday that it was starting "a new chapter beyond New Orleans in 2027" and thanked festival participants and the Crescent City for its hospitality.

In a statement shared with ABC News on Wednesday, a spokesperson for Essence said in part, "We know the people of New Orleans are processing this news. After 32 years, we did not take this decision lightly, but we needed to do what was in the best interest of the community."

The spokesperson said despite the festival generating "more than $300 million in economic impact" for New Orleans, "it has to keep growing for the community it serves." 

"We have been heartened by the overwhelming interest from cities across the country to host the festival's legacy and its future," they added. "We are excited about what is ahead and committed to continuing to make ESSENCE the biggest, most joyful festival for Black culture in the world, and can't wait to share our 2027 Festival plans. To New Orleans: thank you for 32 years."

According to NOLA.com, the online news website for The Times-Picayune, the decision to part ways came after months of failed long-term contract negotiations to keep the festival in the city. The city's previous seven-year contract expired earlier this fall, according to the outlet.

Thousands have since commented on the festival's announcement on Instagram, with several people lamenting the move.

"People don't come to Essence fest just for the festivals they come for the City of New Orleans culture as well," one person commented in part. "Food, music bourbon street. It gives visitors something to do before the concerts."

Another person wrote, "If we can't go to Nola for Essence, where can you go?! It's upsetting me and my homegirls."

Following the festival's announcement, New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno announced in an Instagram video that another "world-class" festival celebrating Black culture will take its place next year.

"Ultimately, we are working to team up with some of this country's top Black producers to essentially bring in a festival that one, realizes how important it is to be in the city of New Orleans, and that the city of New Orleans itself is a draw, but also one that will be able to bring in top talent to perform for you, but also to recognize the amount of talent that we have right here in the city of New Orleans with amazing musicians and artists," Moreno said.

Moreno teased another announcement, coming Dec. 9, that will provide more details and reveal what the new festival will be.

"The festival that we'll be bringing to you will also work to do activations not just in downtown New Orleans, but across the city, from New Orleans East to downtown New Orleans to Algiers," Moreno continued. "And then, of course, we need to make sure that there's widespread benefit for our local businesses, particularly our local Black businesses, when it comes to this festival. And so that's the other piece that we're building as well."

The Essence Festival has drawn celebrities, musicians, superstars and politicians to its celebrations over the years, from former Vice President Kamala Harris and former first lady Michelle Obama to Grammy-winning singer Miguel.

The 2026 Essence Festival took place this past July at the New Orleans Ernest N. Morial Convention Center and the Caesars Superdome and featured performers including Brandy, Monica, Kehlani, Latto, Cardi B., T.I., Patti LaBelle, Public Enemy, and George Clinton and Parliament-Funkadelic.

The festival concluded with an Aaliyah tribute performance curated by Missy Elliott, with performances from Mýa, Normani, Chlöe and more.

ABC News has reached out to Mayor Moreno's office for comment.
news.summary: The Essence Festival of Culture is leaving its longtime home of New Orleans after more than 30 years.
news.author: San Francisco,Yi-Jin Yu

news.title: Maddow says Democrats can abolish Electoral College if they 'swing for the fences'
news.text: MS NOW host Rachel Maddow said during an interview on Saturday that getting rid of the Electoral College was "doable" for Democrats if they "swing for the fences." MS NOW's Jacob Soboroff asked Maddow about her thoughts on Democrats getting rid of the system, which has received criticism after the last two Republican presidents won their first elections despite losing the national popular vote. "My whole life, it has been this kind of theoretical, you know, this hypothetical math problem. You know, if ever enough states to speak for 270 electoral votes all got into this agreement, then it would go into effect, and it always just seems so pie in the sky," she said. GOP WIPEOUT GOES FROM BAD TO WORSE AS DEMS QUIETLY SCORE ANOTHER MAJOR WIN WITH BIG RAMIFICATIONS Maddow said she felt it was doable for the Democrats after speaking with Ben Wikler, a Democratic advocate for eliminating the Electoral College. Soboroff and Maddow said that Democrats could use the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, an agreement that makes it so a state will award all of their electoral votes to whichever presidential candidate wins the overall national popular vote — regardless of who actually won the vote inside that individual state. GAVIN NEWSOM EXPRESSES 'OPENNESS' TO PACKING SCOTUS, CALLS ELECTORAL COLLEGE SYSTEM 'PERVERTED' Eighteen states have signed the compact, in addition to Washington, D.C., which means the compact has 222 electoral votes pledged to it — 48 short of the 270 needed to take effect. However, Democrats now control the governor’s office and both chambers of the state legislatures in the swing states of Michigan, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and Nevada. Those legislatures' combined 50 electoral votes would push the compact to 272 and activate it should they vote to sign the compact. PROGRESSIVES UNVEIL $25 MINIMUM WAGE PUSH TO SOLVE AFFORDABILITY CRISIS DESPITE ECONOMIST INFLATION WARNING "There are enough Democratic states right now who have a Democratic trifecta — governor and the full legislature — that puts you way over 270 if they all decided to do it, and you don't need very many states to act right now for that to be operative," Maddow said. "It's doable. I mean, raising the minimum wage is doable. Getting rid of the Electoral College is doable, age limits for Supreme Court justices might be doable. I mean, the Democrats have big majorities and if they decide to swing for the fences, they could do a lot right now." KAMALA HARRIS CALLS TO EXPAND SUPREME COURT, ADD STATES IF DEMS TAKE CONGRESS Former Vice President and 2024 Democratic nominee Kamala Harris called for major institutional changes in October during an interview, which included "changing" the Electoral College. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "I believe that we need to expand the Supreme Court. We need more justices on the Supreme Court so that we can have a court that actually reinforces the spirit and principles behind the Constitution of the United States," Harris told podcast host Keke Palmer. "I believe that we should be pushing for what is possible around changing the Electoral College. Right?" she added. Harris also lost the popular vote in 2024, making her the first Democratic White House candidate to do so in 20 years. The system allocates 538 electors to the 50 states and Washington, D.C. A majority of 270 is needed to win the presidency. Lise Hand: Trump hates women, and the media, and especially women in the media

Trump threw his power in the tech world around this week with the rehiring of Jensen Huang – and managed to be vulgar along the way.

7.01pm, 25 Nov 2026

Share options

IT’S A NAILED-ON racing certainty that if perchance some Irish business bigwig had hurriedly exited from his top job for – shall we say – ‘conduct unbecoming’, only to be suddenly and inexplicably reinstated, the Taoiseach of the day would not celebrate by posting an AI-generated meme of an event at which someone died violently, featuring the triumphant bigwig holding aloft a bra.

If such a repulsive and bizarre image did pop up in a Taoiseach’s social media feed, the immediate assumption would be that his account had been hacked. And then, upon discovering that it had indeed been created by our head of government, the tumbrils would rumble up Merrion Street and the (metaphorical) head would be promptly demanded. In jig time he would be an ex-Taoiseach who, to quote Monty Python, had now expired and gone to join the choir invisible.

But just such a meme, for anyone who snatched forty winks on Monday and missed an entire U.S. news cycle, was posted by a jubilant President Trump a short time after the shock announcement that Jensen Huang was returning to his position as CEO of Nvidia.

The fake image of Jensen Huang that was shared by TrumpDonald Trump / Truth Social

Donald Trump / Truth Social / Truth Social

To briefly summarise the chaos: Huang resigned on 12 November after revelations that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy who’d routed embargoed Nvidia chips to Chinese AI companies. Reportedly Huang also had undisclosed relationships with two of his employees, including a vice president who reported directly to him. Cue stock market panic, plunging shares amid tech bro terror that the whole AI malarkey could also shortly do an ex-parrot and start pining for the fjords. So Trump personally put the arm on Nvidia’s board and hey presto Huang was back with a, well, bang.

Not long after the bombshell announcement that the prodigal multibillionaire had returned, the president took to Truth Social, posting an AI slop version of the iconic ‘fight, fight, fight’ image taken in the immediate aftermath of the assassination attempt on him during a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania in 2026. Instead, it was Huang’s face streaked with blood, and in his raised fist was a scarlet-coloured bra.

There was immediate outrage. Some people were aghast, pointing out that one person had been killed that day and that a second victim who had sustained serious injuries in the shooting died just two months ago in September. There was also outrage and unease on Capitol Hill where not everybody was buying into the “move along, nothing spy-related to see here” nonchalance emanating from the White House who were insisting that Huang’s credibility is not only intact but enhanced, even, and that everything’s tickety-boo.

Trump and Jesen Huang at the White House in April 2025.Ken Cedeno / UPI via Alamy

Ken Cedeno / UPI via Alamy / UPI via Alamy

Trump, naturally, didn’t give a monkey’s – au contraire. He and the tech bros and the stock market were immediately en fête. Taking credit for Houdini Huang during a phone call to CNBC, the president exulted: “I think he’s gonna start off at an almost higher level. He’s apologised for the indiscretion. Sex sells, fellas.”

Sex sells, fellas.

Even by the short-fingered vulgarian’s usual low standards, this was grim. The priority was to restart the stuttering stock market gravy-train – a vehicle upon which Nvidia shareholder Trump himself is firmly on board, reportedly making $15m (€13.71 million) in the trillion-bucks rebound. Everything else was irrelevant, collateral damage, useful material for a crudely insulting meme.

Advertisement

But it also served as a grim reminder of just how normalised casual sexism and misogyny have become in Donald Trump’s America – granted, it’s deeply ingrained everywhere, but the US is the poster boy for it.

The fact that the Nvidia CEO has reportedly conducted affairs with two colleagues, not to mention his alleged romance with a woman who has had contact with members of Chinese intelligence, is regarded as a nothingburger is stark – hey, what’s the point of being a bigwig if you can’t enjoy the perks of the job, eh? Ol’ Jensen is some man for one man, here’s a meme to celebrate the return of the horndog, oh wait, let’s stick in a bra!

The White House frat house

The disrespect of women and the degradation of their rights was bad enough in Trump’s first term, but it has worsened this second time around.

The White House is a frat house, doused in eau de machismo and peopled with preposterous figures who have the president’s ear, such as the so-called ‘Secretary of War’ Pete Hegseth who wants women out of the military and who basked in the praise of his boss for doing a “great job” with his anti-DEI drive in getting rid of “woke” generals.

Vice-president JD Vance may have been earmarked for his gig when he sneered during a 2021 interview on Fox News that the U.S. was being run by “a bunch of childless cat ladies who are miserable at their own lives and the choices that they’ve made,” specifically naming Kamala Harris, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Pete Buttigieg, a gay man.

And where to begin with Trump’s on-again-off-again BFF, the planet’s richest man, Elon Musk, who arrived into the White House to take up a key position, trailing multiple sexual misconduct allegations in his wake and pursuing a creepy mission to seed the planet with his offspring (at least 14, to date).

Attacks on female journalists

The Commander-in-Chief, unshackled from the constraints of having to run for office again, routinely attacks journalists who have the audacity to ask what he sees as impertinent questions, which are in fact extremely pertinent – and he’s noticeably more vicious when a woman is in the firing-line, as this sample of recent interactions at press gaggles shows all-too clearly.

To CNN’s Kaitlin Collins: “CNN is a very corrupt organisation with a corrupt reporter standing right there, never smiles, a young beautiful woman never smiles, I see her standing there with hatred in her eyes.”

To CNN’s Kristen Holmes: “No, CNN poll numbers are fake, and your whole outfit is fake, and so are you.”

To Bloomberg’s Catherine Lucey : “Quiet. Quiet, piggy.”

CBS News / YouTube

To ABC’s Mary Bruce: “It’s your attitude. I think you are a terrible reporter. It’s the way you ask these questions… a horrible, insubordinate question.”

To NBC’s Yamiche Alcindor, who is Black: “I know you don’t see dirt, but if you take a look at the White House, you’d never notice broken windows, obviously, from where you come… But we had 18 broken windows.”

To CNN’s Kristen Holmes: “Someday, your children will come across your disgusting and inhumane question. They will be sickened and embarrassed to have a parent be so callous and vindictive. It’s quite troubling.”

To NBC’s Monica Alba: ““Quiet! You’re a horrible little reporter, aren’t you?”

Commenting on a question by ABC’s Karen Travers: “I had one woman from ‘ABC Fake News’, one of the worst of all… this woman starts screaming.

I recognise her immediately – not a particularly attractive person, inside or out.

“In fact, I just am amazed that these people can be reporters or anchors. She’s screaming. She’s a nasty person.”

On NYT’s Maggie Haberman: “Maggot Hagerman, the Fake Reporter from The Failing New York Times, an unattractive person both inside and out, and who knows less about me than most reporters on the beat (She’s a SCAMMER!).”

Such sexist bullying rarely causes a ripple anymore. It’s shrugged off. Just Trump being Trump.

CNN / YouTube

The glass cliff

His anger towards women is always ready to bubble over; despite various male members of his inner circle such as FBI director Kash Patel, Robert Kennedy Jr. and Hegseth becoming embroiled in various controversies and bad calls, the figures being ejected through the Oval Office’s swing doors are almost all female. And most have been replaced by men.

Most recently, his chief of staff Susan Wiles was replaced by hard-right zealot Stephen Miller, and also this term Trump has fired or pushed out at least half a dozen top women including Attorney General Pam Bondi, Labour Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer, Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, and White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia. (Zacharia announced the departure of Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle from the White House podium – the only news she would share, it turned out – a mere three days before she too was handed her P45.) Moreover, Zacharia was replacing Karoline Leavitt who had ceded the position of faithful presidential guard dog to the Stepford Printer, Trump’s deeply weird executive assistant Natalie Harp.

Trump now floats in a dangerous bubble of he-men and yes-men and subordinate women who know their place. In his social milieu, he’s surrounded by women who have literally moulded themselves into his preferred aesthetic of ‘Mar-A-Lago face’, best described as high, dark, arched brows; cartoonishly inflated lips; skin frozen and pulled tautly over multiple syringes’ worth of filler; and barely open eyes that appear to have been pulled sideways and up. Mere coincidence? A quick search for images of philanthropist Susan Dell, Callista Gingrich, wife of Newt Gingrich, far-right activist Laura Loomer and the above-mentioned Kimberly Guilfoyle, would suggest otherwise.

All of it makes for a depressing vista.

But maybe there’s a sliver of hope – as a result of the midterm Blue tsunami, the Democrats will have over 100 women serving in Congress for the first time and perhaps they can begin to recalibrate the gender power imbalance.

But judging by Huang’s unsettling Houdini act, it looks like the broligarchy won’t cede ground without a fight, fight, fight.

news.title: 'The View' Co-Host Ana Navarro Slams Democrats Who Insist Party Must Nominate a White Man in 2028
news.text:
Ana Navarro erupted in an expletive-filled rant over Democrats pushing for a white male to be top of the presidential ticket in 2028, RadarOnline.com can reveal. 

The 54-year-old The View panelist noted that some within the party want to go that route after both Hillary Clinton and Kamala Harris suffered losses to Donald Trump in 2016 and 2024. However, Joe Biden managed to topple the tycoon in the 2020 race for the White House.Ana Navarro Attempts to Take Break From 'Insanity of Our Political World'The CNN political pundit opened the Monday, November 23, episode of her Bleep! With Ana Navarro podcast by promising she'd lay off the heavy political talk that usually dominates the program. 

"This week is Thanksgiving, so I wanted to take a break from the dysfunction and insanity of our political world, and I wanted us to have a little fun," she told viewers while introducing her guests, actor-comedians Anthony Anderson and Cedric the Entertainer.

But Navarro then turned to the 2028 presidential race and said some people in the Democratic Party want a "white man" to run against the GOP's nominee for the White House.Ana Navarro Thinks Dems Are 'Scarred' From Kamala Harris and Hillary Clinton's Losses to Trump"You know, there's all this talk of whether Kamala Harris should run again or should not run again. And I hear people saying, 'No, this time we've got to nominate a white man,' because I think people are scarred, are scarred from the fact that two very qualified women, Hillary Clinton and Kamala Harris, lost against the most unqualified human being that has ever set foot in the Oval Office," Navarro huffed, referring to the longtime career politicians' losses to real estate mogul Trump. 

"But it p----- me off to hear that said. And I'm hearing it from women, and I'm hearing it from Black women, and I'm hearing it from feminist women and liberal women who supported Kamala, who supported Hillary, because again, I think people are scarred," she explained.'We've Got to Keep Trying'Anderson asked Navarro, "Do you honestly think that the world that we live in here in the United States, do you think they are willing to have a female in the most powerful chair in the world? Do you think we're willing to do that?"

"I don't know. But I think we've got to keep trying," the political commentator fired back. "I mean, I don't want to tell little Black girls and little brown girls that they are out of the game from the start just because of the color of their skin or their gender. So, if they're qualified, h--- yes."Kamala Harris' Earliest Political Backer Urging Her Not to Run in 2028Despite her 2024 defeat to Trump, Harris, 62, is reportedly weighing another White House bid in 2028. But one of her earliest political backers has urged the former vice president to abandon her comeback dreams, and his objections have nothing to do with her being a woman.

"I'm sorry that she even thinks about running for president. I don't want her to run," California political kingpin and Harris ex-boyfriend Willie Brown told The Red Letter's Tara Palmeri on November 23, but said it has nothing to do with her qualifications since "She’s reached the highest electoral level for any woman in America."

Brown, 92, took aim at Harris' struggles to connect with voters during the 2024 presidential election, suggesting her "word salads" left Americans scratching their heads over where she actually stood on key issues.

"She's not a communicator," he declared. "No Baptist preacher flavor in her soul."
news.summary: 'The View' panelist thinks some Dems are 'scarred' by Hillary Clinton and Kamala Harris' crushing losses to Donald Trump.

news.title: Influencers Behaving Badly at No 10? Burnham could have worse problems | Emma Brockes
news.text:
These are dangerous times to be a prime minister. So it is perhaps reassuring that the trouble into which Andy Burnham barrelled this week is so old school as to be almost soothing. Four months into his premiership, Burnham has arrived early at that rite of passage: the catastrophic attempt to engage with popular culture and subsequent category-5 storm in a teacup. After footage emerged of Influencers Behaving Badly at Downing Street, Burnham, in my view, has come out of the whole thing in surprisingly good shape.

To recap: earlier this month, Burnham held a reception for social media influencers, one of whom, Luke Hamnett, was permitted to film himself doing the Hugh Grant dance from Love Actually before sitting down to interview the prime minister. Meanwhile, self-described “presenter, podcaster, idiot” Max Balegde filmed himself outside the door of No 10 miming what, in the words of the Daily Mail as it geared up to go the full Judge Pickles, “appeared to be a viral meme song”. These words were “bomboclaat pussywagon chicken nuggets”, which, as the Telegraph took a breath from its own meltdown to explain, turns on “a Jamaican profanity popularised online”.

If you can absorb any of these details without laughing like a drain, you are a more serious person than me. But in any case, it isn’t the content so much as what the influencers represent that has launched Burnham’s opponents into orbit. I’m not familiar with the line “bomboclaat pussywagon chicken nuggets”, but for those of us with young children, it is instantly recognisable as the latest contribution to the “skibidi toilet” meme tradition of conjoining rude words a 10-year-old would find funny and putting them on endless repeat. This would be more embarrassing for Burnham were it not for one fact: between them, Balegde and Hamnett have more than six million followers across Instagram and TikTok, substantially more than the Daily Telegraph. We can be confident the average age of those followers is not 61.

Data as provoking as this obviously calls for a full-throated overreaction, and Kemi Badenoch didn’t disappoint. On Tuesday, the Tory leader requested an apology from the prime minister for turning No 10 into “his personal studio to carry out these silly TikToks”. All right, grandma! She went on to point out that, assuming Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping had watched these videos, enemies of the UK would “see that our prime minister is not a serious man and they will think we are not a serious country”. I have to say this was my favourite part of the whole saga, evoking as it did the tail lights of a ship that sailed decades ago when we elected a former head of communications at Carlton TV, David Cameron, followed by fake model-bus enthusiast Boris Johnson and highly perishable Liz Truss to the top job in this very serious nation. Good one, Kemi!

Meanwhile, Burnham himself had to put a certain amount of damage limitation into place. While it stopped short of an apology, it did involve a spokesperson calling the Balegde video “clearly not acceptable” and it being removed from the influencer’s account. And just when you thought it couldn’t get any better, up popped Nigel Farage with what read to me like a very ambivalent condemnation, indicating that he too – and it pains me to say this, since it plays in his favour – had found the whole thing hilarious. “I wouldn’t let them behave quite the way that it happened,” he said when asked if, were he prime minister, he’d invite influencers to Downing Street. “It showed a slight lack of respect for the place and for the office and was really very inappropriate indeed.” Lot of qualifiers in that statement, Nigel; we can hear you laughing from here.

For the rest of us, I suspect Influencergate has provided a brief, luminous break from real news. If it has a vibe of Michael Crawford on runaway skates flying down a hill – to cite a reference followers of Hamnett and Balegde probably won’t get – there is also a serious part: it’s entirely sensible for Burnham to court influencers in an effort to engage young people in politics. As a cautionary tale, we might look to the US and the disastrous decision made by Kamala Harris during the last presidential election not to appear on Joe Rogan’s podcast and talk to parts of the country old media can’t reach.

In Burnham’s case, the charge isn’t that he sucked up to political enemies, but rather that he engaged in a puff piece at the expense of more robust political interviews. (Hamnett opened the encounter with the remark: “I’m so proud you’re prime minister”, and it got friendlier from there.) And yet there’s no indication the prime minister will stop talking to higher-end hacks and, for my money, he has come out on top – partly for the sheer entertainment value of watching the Tories try to grab the moral high ground and partly because of a quality in Burnham himself.

At the top of Hamnett’s interview, with a bloody great neon sign advertising his podcast jammed into the Downing Street fireplace and the influencer sitting there in slacks, (Prada!) trainers and a daffy look, you can see something happening in Burnham’s expression. It advances, slowly, from affable, to sheepish, to what looks to me like an “oh, God” moment when he understands there’s a good chance all this nonsense will go south. Ironically, it’s the thing politicians dream of; an instant in which the audience, with a smile, thinks we can all relate to that.

 Emma Brockes is a Guardian columnist

news.title: Democrats to include creators and influencers to maximize viewership for presidential primary debates
news.text: The Democratic Party announced on Monday that its upcoming presidential primary debate process will include "creators and influencers," sparking excitement on the left and mockery from conservatives. The Democrats announced 12 debates starting in June 2027, and candidates must denounce dark money spending in the primary in order to access the debate stage. The DNC added that it will "seek to maximize the viewership of the debates" by incorporating content creators and influencers, as many popular online personalities draw massive audiences. Ben Tyson, co-founder of Good Fight Political, a Democratic campaign firm, said it’s a "great step" by the DNC to include creators and influencers when determining the 2028 presidential nominee. "I'm excited to see them take steps to broaden and modernize the media reach of the upcoming primary debates. It's still too early to know for sure what this will look like exactly, but the big picture is more important than the details to me. Generating an effective narrative in today's media ecosystem requires a recognition of the connectivity between legacy and social media, which is exactly what this effort seems primed to accomplish," Tyson told Fox News Digital. HASAN PIKER MAKES AOC HIS 2028 PICK FOR PRESIDENT, SAYS IT'S 'NOT EVEN A QUESTION’ It’s unclear which creators and influencers will be involved, but far-left streamer Hasan Piker, as well as far-left journalists Mehdi Hasan and Ryan Grim, have each expressed interest. Tyson cited Reuters Institute's 2026 Digital News Report that found 77% of adults globally watch online news videos every week, largely on platforms like YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook. "Social media is the new home of legacy press content, and for a narrative to truly penetrate to voters, it requires harnessing traditional press to write about it, and then getting creators and everyday users need to share and promote it," Tyson said. "So, whether it ends up being questions from local creators and influencers, bringing them into the audience, or all the way to having creator partnerships in moderating and hosting debates, I'm glad to see the DNC is meeting the moment and bringing a modern media approach to the upcoming presidential primary," Tyson continued. Tyson said the DNC completely revamped its approach to social media for the 2026 campaign, generating more than 13 billion views from thousands of posts, reaching five times as many users as in 2024, and building a clip-sharing network of more than 700 creators, according to the party’s post-election recap. "This looks like another positive step to continue building on that work," Tyson said. "From our perspective, we actively encourage the campaigns we work with to include clipping and creator outreach as fundamentals in their media toolkits, including working with real-life streamers to try to proactively generate this earned media feedback loop that we see in the most prominent campaigns across the country." INSIDE HASAN PIKER’S RADICAL VIEWS ON AMERICA, ISRAEL AND SOCIALISM Heritage Action media fellow Tim Young, who has over 1.1 million followers on X alone, feels Democrats will botch the primary process if social media influencers are too involved. "The last few times Democrats went hard in on influencers, we saw a woman famous for taking a bath in a bathtub full of Froot Loops interview Barack Obama, we saw a trans woman topless on the White House lawn, and we saw an interesting intern in a dress with long fingernails," Young told Fox News Digital. "I can only imagine the lack of seriousness that the Democrat Party will have in their debate schedule," Young continued. "Especially when the last time there was a primary election, their nominee, Vice President Kamala Harris, didn’t receive a single vote on her pathway to ‘victory.’" Indeed, GloZell Green was widely known for a "Froot Loop Challenge" when she interviewed then-President Obama in 2015, transgender content creator Rose Montoya was banned from White House events after posing topless on the South Lawn during a Pride Month event hosted by then-President Joe Biden, and Gen Z influencer Benito Skinner promoted the COVID-19 vaccine alongside former White House press secretary Jen Psaki. HASAN PIKER IS BECOMING THE 'FACE OF THE PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT,' FORMER DEMOCRATIC OPERATIVE WARNS Despite backlash to all three stunts, Young doesn’t expect Democrats to pivot on the heels of the blue tsunami that occurred during the midterm elections. "Their current strategy wins, so get ready for whatever the unserious circus may be," Young said. Former DNI chief of staff Alexa Henning doesn’t anticipate the Democrats' social media approach to be particularly successful, either. "Democrats looking at 2024 and deciding they need more influencers is what happens when everyone in the strategy meeting wants an invitation to the same parties. It failed then, it’ll fail again," Henning told Fox News Digital. The 2028 field is considered wide-open, with possible candidates including Kamala Harris again, as well as figures like California Gov. Gavin Newsom, former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio Cortez, D-N.Y., Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., and Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro, among many others. As Americans wait for details to emerge, Media Research Center president David Bozell offered a prediction. "The real debate will happen before the debates, when 400 influencers are knifing each other over 12 press passes," Bozell told Fox News Digital. The DNC did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE DNC Chair Ken Martin provided the following statement when announcing the debate plans: "Democrats are on offense after our historic victories in the midterms, and the DNC is keeping our foot on the gas as we head into the 2028 cycle. The fair and transparent process and experienced leadership team we’re announcing today will keep our party united, strengthen our eventual nominee, and put Democrats in position to take back the White House." The first two debates will occur in June and July 2027 with the final debate scheduled for March 2028. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
news.summary: The Democratic Party will add creators and influencers to 12 primary debates starting in 2027, but conservatives like Tim Young predict a circus.

news.title: Even if Schumer Wins, He Loses
news.text:
Even if Schumer wins that vote, he may lose in the long run.

According to recent reports, Schumer has 14 public backers, including himself, and Van Hollen claims to have about 15, but only five on record. The winner needs 29 votes. Senate Democrats will cast secret ballots to choose the leader.

Van Hollen's early backers are the radicals, of course, including two senators-elect, Minnesota's Peggy Flanagan and Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed. El-Sayed reached the Senate by beating Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.), Schumer's pick, in the Michigan Democrat primary.

But the movement against Schumer is growing, and goes beyond Congress.

The New York Times reported that about 35 entertainers signed a letter urging Senate Democrats to dump Schumer. The names include Jane Fonda, Robert De Niro, Chelsea Handler, Marisa Tomei, Padma Lakshmi, TV producer David Mandel, and comedian Jon Stewart.

ICYMI: John Kennedy Savages El-Sayed Again, and Nobody Does It Quite Like Him

Actor Mark Ruffalo is actually promoting a phone bank for the campaign to replace Schumer with Van Hollen. The event description praised Van Hollen's support for Medicare for All, a wealth tax on billionaires, ending military aid to Israel, and getting money out of politics.

That's the agenda driving the anti-Schumer push.

Ruffalo said Democrats need leaders who follow "the will of the people not entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties."

Israel is just one issue in a whole host of reasons Van Hollen is the right leader for our times. We need Justice , we need leadership that follows the will of the people not entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties. Does not follow entrenched fossil fuel and corporate…— Mark Ruffalo (@MarkRuffalo) November 21, 2026

Given that Schumer is Jewish, critics including ADL CEO Jonathan Greenblatt, Coalition for Jewish Values Executive Vice President Rabbi Yaakov Menken, and Meghan McCain called the remark antisemitic.

Schumer may be favored in this election due to his leadership status, but the radical, antisemitic left is calling the shots in the party now, and the vote is by secret ballot, so senators can promise Schumer one thing and do another. And, let’s face it, the activist pressure gives them every incentive to do so.

Democrat voters are another problem for Chuck. A fresh Economist/YouGov poll found that 40% of Democrats want Van Hollen leading Senate Democrats, while just 19% picked Schumer, a stunning 21-point gap. Among those who voted for Kamala Harris in 2024, the gap widens to 30 points, with 48% for Van Hollen and 18% for Schumer.

Economist/YouGov poll | 11/20-11/23Who would you rather have as the leader of the Democrats in the US Senate?(Democrats sampled)🟦Chris Van Hollen: 40%🟦Chuck Schumer: 19%——(2024 Kamala Harris voters)🟦Chris Van Hollen: 48%🟦Chuck Schumer: 18% https://t.co/5bfrDXySX3 pic.twitter.com/V6NjIbLsRn— Politics & Poll Tracker 📡 (@PollTracker2024) November 24, 2026

Even if Schumer ekes out a victory, his political capital in the Democrat Party is shot. Leading a party whose own voters prefer the other guy by more than 2 to 1 is a far harder job, and every senator weighing a future primary knows it.

Schumer has led Senate Democrats since 2016 and still hasn't said whether he'll seek reelection in 2028. No matter how the leadership election turns out, he'll emerge severely weakened. Democrats have spent years feeding their activist base, and they’re learning the hard way that the base expects to run the show.

news.title: ROOKE: Gov. Sanders Can’t Lead GOP With Her Massive Blind Spot On Young Men
news.text:
Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders seems to be vying for power within the Republican Party, but she can’t even find a way out of the mess she created. 

In September, Sanders released a midterm ad painting young white men as the face of the welfare state. She then appeared on screen telling voters they shouldn’t have to subsidize healthy adults who “just choose not to work.” Almost instantly, the ad was denounced as out of touch with reality and disrespectful towards young, white men who are a critical voting bloc for Republicans. Like most elected officials, she refused to see reason, defending the ad, claiming that any criticism was connected to her welfare work requirement and not the terrible way she painted young men. 

Sanders still seems not to have absorbed the central lesson of the 2026 midterms or the backlash of her welfare ad. In a Sunday interview with the Daily Signal, Sanders was asked about the contentious ad. She dismissed the criticisms, immediately pivoting to parroting her line about how “able-bodied adults” shouldn’t receive welfare, framing the condemnation as something that “seems to go against everything that conservatives have been pushing for.”

She’s had months and a terrible GOP election night to reflect on her original response, as well as ample time to decide how she’d respond if a journalist asked her about it. She, of course, knows that the critics objected to the specific choice of casting a young white male gamer as the representative face of welfare dependency. And yet she continues to treat the entire episode as a fight over work requirements and not the actual issue. The criticism against her did not reject her policy of requiring work or training to access welfare. By refusing to acknowledge this was a rejection of her portrayal of young men, Sanders signals to her gala-going friends that she’s still a “safe” Republican. 

“Don’t worry, friends. I’m not going to talk about anything that truly matters.”

The optics and accuracy of the messaging do not matter to her. It’s of no significance to her that young white men are among the lowest-rate groups on major welfare programs. Nationally and in her home state of Arkansas, participation rates in SNAP and Medicaid are higher among black and Hispanic adults than whites. Yes, it’s accurate to state that white Americans form a majority of caseloads in Arkansas, but that is simply because the state is roughly 70 percent white. The catch is that the rate at which they enroll is still lower. Even more embarrassing for Sanders is the fact that childless young men, especially young white men like the one portrayed in her ad, are actually a small minority of recipients. (Sign up for Mary Rooke’s weekly newsletter here!)

And before you ask why this ad matters so much, it’s important to take a look at just how badly Republicans did with young men during the midterm elections. The same demographic (young men) that delivered decisive support for Republicans in 2024 abandoned them in 2026.

CIRCLE’s analysis of AP VoteCast data found that young men ages 18-29 backed President Donald Trump over former Vice President Kamala Harris 56 percent to 42 percent in 2024. Young white men did so by an even greater margin, supporting Trump 63 percent to Kamala’s 35 percent. That is a decisive shellacking thanks to what could have been a generational voting bloc, but Republicans squandered it. CIRCLE’s analysis of NORC Civic Health and Elections Project data from the 2026 midterms shows young men supporting Democratic House candidates by 22 points. Young white men in particular went from a 28-point Republican advantage to an 11-point Democratic advantage in one election. Not just that, but overall young voter turnout fell off a cliff. 

Now you can’t blame this shift on Sanders’ ad alone. But combine it with Trump breaking his promise not to start new wars and the state of the economy pushing the American Dream farther away from them than ever before, and the election data becomes understandable to any reasonable person watching. However, to Sanders, it seems to have flown over her head once again. 

Days after the midterms, she posted a New York Post headline claiming “shell-shocked Republicans were looking to [her] for the blueprint on how to resurrect the party.” The story praised her 15-point reelection margin, which, to be fair in this election cycle, was impressive. However, it immediately went off the rails, noting her defense of the Iran War. Interestingly, it made no mention of the ad or the collapse among the young male voters, which, of course, means it also didn’t include her plan to win them back. (RELATED: GOP Misreads The Midterms, While Democrats Are Adjusting Their Playbook)

She so desperately wants to be treated as a national model for Republican victory, but she fails the most basic test. No serious observer of the midterm elections is turning to the governor who spent precious political capital demonizing the very voters the GOP needs and refuses to understand her mistake.

news.title: Kamala Harris's Former Mentor and Lover Willie Brown Delivers Savage Warning Over 2028 Comeback — 'I Don't Want Her To Run'
news.text:
Kamala Harris has been warned against running for presidency in 2028 by her former mentor and lover Willie Brown.

RadarOnline.com can reveal the longtime political California powerbroker, 92, says he's "sorry" Harris, 62, is even considering launching a fresh campaign after her election defeat to Donald Trump in 2024.'She Clearly Was Very Hurt'Brown said: "I'm sorry that she even thinks about running for president. I don't want her to run.

"She clearly was very hurt."

The former Sam Francisco mayor, who dated Harris in the mid-‘90s when she was 29 and he was 60, has previously questioned her communication skills, suggesting she lacks the qualities needed to connect with voters.

Brown was particularly dismissive of her ability to command an audience, saying she had no "Baptist preacher flavor in her soul," suggesting she lacked the natural communication style and charisma needed to win over voters.Brown Told Harris To Pursue Career Outside Of PoliticsHe also said Harris had already reached the highest elected position held by a woman in America, referring to her four years as vice president under former President Joe Biden, encouraging her to pursue opportunities outside politics.

Brown spoke about his relationship in 2019, telling the San Francisco Chronicle: "Yes, we dated. It was more than 20 years ago. Yes, I may have influenced her career by appointing her to two state commissions when I was Assembly speaker.

"And I certainly helped with her first race for district attorney in San Francisco. I have also helped the careers of House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, Gov. Gavin Newsom, Sen. Dianne Feinstein and a host of other politicians."'I Go Back And Forth'The former Veep has not officially announced plans for 2028, though she chose not to run for California governor last year, keeping her options open for a possible presidential bid. 

In April, she revealed in a CNN interview that she had not made up her mind, saying: "I go back and forth."

Harris said that if she does launch another campaign, she'll be "very specific" in her approach. It would be her third bid for the White House, after the 2020 primary and her 2024 general election loss to Trump.

"If I run, my motivation is not to beat other Democrats," she said. "It's to actually do the job.""I’m sure there are many who think that I should just sit at home and eat bonbons and cook Doug’s favorite foods,” she said, pointing to a recent Wall Street Journal report that her husband, Doug Emhoff, privately told some people that he preferred she didn’t run. "I could cook Doug's favorite foods and do this."

Harris added: "I feel so strongly and therefore am compelled, and maybe propelled, into doing this, because I know that I can help. 

"And how can I sit at home in the comfort of my home when I know there are things I can do to help? I don’t know any other life but that — that’s my point. I don’t know any life that is not about, 'There’s a problem, what can I do to fix it?'"
news.summary: Kamala Harris has been warned against running for presidency in 2028 by former mentor and lover Willie Brown, who previously hit out at her communication skills.
